h: Before You Pick Up Your Arrows
p: King Street is one of those Manchester streets that rewards looking up. The buildings along it are grand old banking halls and offices, and plenty now house smart shops and restaurants, so even the walk to the oche feels like a bit of an occasion. It's central enough that you can reach it on foot from Piccadilly or Victoria stations, and the Metrolink stops at St Peter's Square and Exchange Square are close by too.

Groups tend to get the most out of it when they treat the darts as the centrepiece rather than an afterthought. Book a slot that fits your group size, let everyone order a drink and get settled, then let the games do the work. Total beginners often surprise themselves, because the formats reward the odd lucky throw as much as skill. If anyone wants a quick tip, stand side-on, keep the throwing elbow still and follow through towards the board.

Want to tack on some culture before your session? The John Rylands Library on Deansgate is a stunning neo-Gothic building with a reading room that looks like something out of a fantasy film, and Manchester Art Gallery on Mosley Street is free to wander round. Central Library on St Peter's Square is worth a peek too.
Allow a couple of hours if you're eating as well, and leave yourself time to wander afterwards. Manchester's city centre doesn't really do quiet evenings.
